misconceptions.description: Judging a generated image by how realistic or detailed it looks rather than by whether it represents the to-be-learned relationship clearly
misconceptions.trigger: learner prefers a richly rendered scene over a simpler diagram that shows the target relationship
misconceptions.feedback: Ask what the image must teach. Decorative detail can add extraneous load. The best instructional image shows the relationship, not the most pixels.

misconceptions.description: Assuming an unrelated or seductive generated image is harmless because it looks engaging
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds a vivid but off-topic image to make the screen lively
misconceptions.feedback: Seductive detail can divert attention from the essential. If the image does not carry the learning point, it competes with it.

misconceptions.description: Treating a generated instructional image as factually correct without checking it against the content source
misconceptions.trigger: learner ships a generated diagram with miscounted parts or wrong labels because it looked authoritative
misconceptions.feedback: Generated images can render confident but wrong content. Verify every label, count, and relationship against the source before use.

misconceptions.description: Believing a clever prompt alone makes the image instructionally sound, skipping the design judgment about what the learner needs
misconceptions.trigger: learner refines wording for style but never states the learning function the image must serve
misconceptions.feedback: Start from the learning function, then prompt toward it. A vivid prompt with no instructional target produces decoration.
